title: Defensive downstream patterns: KV/stream/DB throttling, conn-pool tuning, and staged degradation
creator: Marcus Lee
description:
Objective: Harden Redwood inference runtime against transient and sustained downstream failures (Redis/KV, Kafka streams, Postgres/OLTP) by implementing defensive patterns: adaptive connection pooling, circuit breakers with hysteresis, load-shedding policies, and staged degradation modes. This ticket defines the design, implementation plan, and rollout steps for service-side changes + observability required to meet SLOs under degraded downstream conditions.

Scope:
- Connection pool behavior and backpressure for Redis (prefix/KV cache) and Postgres replicas.
- Circuit breaker thresholds and state machine for Kafka producer/consumer and KV reads.
- Load-shedding rules at ingress and internal service boundaries (token-bucket for best-effort requests, prioritized queues for critical paths).
- Degradation modes: read-only, stale-cache serving with TTL grace, reduced model sampling (latency-conserving), and async fallback for non-blocking ops.
- Monitoring, SLI/SLO adjustments, and runbook/alerting changes.

Non-goals: Changes to external downstream infra (e.g., provisioning more Redis instances) and client-side SDK rate limiting (separate SDK work).
acceptance_criteria: Connection pools (Redis/Postgres) implement configurable max-conns, wait queues with bounded timeouts, and metrics emitted for wait-latency and queue-overflow.
Circuit breakers for KV and Kafka trip at configurable error-rate and latency thresholds and expose current state (closed/open/half-open) via runtime metrics and /health endpoints.

Load-shedding layer enforces per-route priorities; under overload, low-priority requests are rejected with 429 and a structured retry-after header; high-priority requests maintain 95th percentile latency SLO within 20% of baseline.
Degradation staging implemented: 1) attempt fast-path (in-memory/stale-cache); 2) fallback to async write queue for best-effort telemetry; 3) fail closed for critical writes with clear error codes.
Dashboards and alerts created: downstream-error-rate, connpool-waiters, shed-rate-by-route, cb-state-transitions. Runbook updated with step-by-step recovery and failover instructions.
Integration tests that simulate Redis/Kafka/Postgres tail-latency spikes validate that circuit breakers open and that latency-sensitive endpoints remain within degradation SLAs.
tasks: Draft design doc and run through reliability guild review (design doc: https://confluence.redwood/team/runtime/downstream-failsafes).
Implement conn-pool instrumentation and bounded wait queues (runtime repo PR #2789).
Add circuit breaker library bindings and default policies for KV/Kafka; expose state metrics.
Implement ingress load-shedding middleware with configurable priorities and token-bucket policy.
Create degraded-mode handlers: stale-cache TTL grace, read-only gate, async write queue and backlog monitor.
Add e2e chaos tests (redis-kill, kafka-throttle, pg-high-latency) and CI step to assert SLO behavior.
Create dashboards, alerts, and runbook; coordinate on-call training for new failure modes.
decisions: Use a small in-house circuit-breaker implementation (licensed MIT) integrated into the runtime to keep telemetry minimal; avoid full Hystrix-like dependency.
Conn-pool strategy: prefer conservative max-conns per worker and bounded wait queue with exponential backoff and jitter; reject requests after configurable timeout to avoid herd pressure.
Load-shedding policy: priority-based with explicit route labels (critical, normal, best-effort); default best-effort for background telemetry and long-tail batch ops.
Degradation order: prefer serving possibly-stale cached responses to blocking on slow downstreams for latency-sensitive endpoints.
updates: 2026-02-28: Initial ticket created after on-call incident 2026-02-25 where Redis tail latency caused request pileup and elevated 99p latencies. Included initial notes from incident review.
2026-03-01: Design review with reliability guild — agreed on staged degradation and observability requirements. Action: Priya to prototype conn-pool metrics by 2026-03-04.

2026-03-04: Prototype PR opened for conn-pool instrumentation: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2789. Basic metrics (waiters, timeouts, active_conns) added. Feedback from Evan: add histogram for wait latency and tag by endpoint.
2026-03-05: Added initial circuit breaker thresholds proposal into design doc; recommended default: open when 5xx rate > 3% over 2m and 95th latency > 1s for 30s window. Needs SLO alignment.
notes: Keep client-facing error codes stable (429 for shed, 503 for service-unavailable) and document SDK retry semantics. Coordinate with PM for messaging and customer communication plan if a rollout toggles shed defaults.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: conn-pool metrics + circuit breaker library (week 1). Phase 2: ingress load-shed middleware + degraded handlers (week 2). Phase 3: e2e chaos tests and dashboards, gradual rollout to staging then prod with feature flags. Feature flag keys: cb-kv-enabled, shed-priority-v1, degraded-mode-ttl.
risks: Aggressive shedding may cause client-visible errors for legitimate traffic — requires careful priority mapping and rollback knobs.
Incorrect circuit-breaker thresholds can either trip too early (causing unnecessary fail-open behavior) or too late (no protection).
Async write backlog could grow unbounded if downstream stays unhealthy — need hard quota and monitoring.
